Accounts

Patient vs. doctor

What changes after you log in depends on which account type you registered as.

Patient

Registers with basic details, then lands on their own dashboard.

  1. Register or log in
  2. Land on the patient dashboard
  3. Fill a new case, or open a past one

Doctor

Registers separately from patients, then reviews submitted cases.

  1. Register or log in
  2. Land on the doctor dashboard
  3. Open any patient's case and its Analysis
Questions

Good to know

Why is the intake form split into sections?

Long clinical forms are easy to abandon halfway through. Short, related sections keep each screen quick to finish and make it easy to pick back up if a patient gets interrupted.

Can a patient see their own past cases?

Yes — the patient dashboard keeps a history of previously submitted forms, so a returning patient doesn't have to fill everything in again.

What does a doctor see that a patient doesn't?

Doctors get the review side of the app: a dashboard listing patient cases, and the Analysis report for each one. Patients can't see other patients' cases.

Is this the full SIH problem statement yet?

Not yet — the current build covers structured intake, case review, and role-based dashboards. Voice-based conversational intake, OCR document upload, AI-generated summaries, and ABDM/ABHA integration are the next pieces planned.
